title: Thematic Analysis Coding Laboratory
summary: One invented interview extract. The learner writes a code of their own, then sets it beside three defensible coding passes over the same words. Nothing is marked, no agreement is computed, and the page says why agreement is not the criterion for this method.
learningObjectives: Describe coding as an analytic act rather than an extraction from a transcript.
Explain why two competent analysts producing different codes is the expected case.
Distinguish semantic, latent and critical readings of the same extract.
State what a given reading brings forward and what it pushes out of view.
Explain why inter-rater agreement is not the criterion for reflexive thematic analysis.
interactionTypes: free-text coding with no answer key
the learners own code echoed back without evaluation
three defensible passes over the same words, each with what it costs
a reflexive prompt inside the feedback
privacy: Nothing is collected, stored or transmitted.
accessibilityNotes: Keyboard operable throughout, with a free-text area sized for a few words rather than an essay. Nothing the learner writes is marked, scored or compared. The three passes are presented as text blocks with their codes as a list and their trade-offs as labelled boxes, so nothing depends on colour or position. No timed content and no motion.
dataStatus: Fictional. The extract is invented for teaching and no participant, interview, institution or study is represented. Anything typed stays in the tab and is neither stored nor transmitted.
simulationNotes: The three passes are semantic, staying close to what is said; latent, reading for what the speaker is doing; and critical, reading for the setting that makes this sayable. They are three positions on a continuum, chosen to make the range visible rather than to exhaust it: a narrative, psychosocial or feminist reading would produce others again. The activity never marks a code, never computes agreement between codings, and never evaluates what the learner wrote.
readmeTopic: coding as an analytic act, and why competent analysts differ
